business_scenario: List bank customers categorized in the Premium customer segment.

business_scenario: Calculate the average account balance across all retail banking accounts.

business_scenario: Find the largest single transaction amount processed in transactions.

business_scenario: Count distinct customer branch cities represented in the banking ledger.
solution_approach: I will count the distinct city values in customers.

business_scenario: Return settled transactions with status Completed for ledger reconciliation.
solution_approach: I will keep transactions whose status is Completed.

answer_sql: SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE status = 'Completed';

business_scenario: Classify accounts into High, Medium, or Low balance tiers based on account balance.
solution_approach: I will use CASE on balance with 100000 and 50000 boundaries.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT account_id, balance, CASE WHEN balance >= 100000 THEN 'High' WHEN balance >= 50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS amount_band FROM accounts ORDER BY account_id;

business_scenario: Find Active customer accounts with a balance of at least 50000 eligible for premium debit card benefits.
solution_approach: I will require Active status and balance of at least 50000.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE status = 'Active' AND balance >= 50000;

business_scenario: Show each customers name with its accounts details.
solution_approach: I will join customers to accounts using customer id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_name, r.account_id, r.status, r.balance FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id ORDER BY m.customer_id,r.account_id;

business_scenario: Count accounts for every account products item.
solution_approach: I will left join account products to accounts by product id. I will group each account products item and count matching accounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.product_name, COUNT(r.account_id) AS record_count FROM account_products c LEFT JOIN accounts r ON c.product_id=r.product_id GROUP BY c.product_id,c.product_name ORDER BY c.product_id;

business_scenario: Find accounts that have no transactions.
solution_approach: I will left join transactions to accounts on account id and keep accounts with a null transaction id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.account_id FROM accounts r LEFT JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id WHERE e.transaction_id IS NULL ORDER BY r.account_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total event amount for each accounts.
solution_approach: I will join accounts to transactions using account id. I will group by account id and sum event amounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.account_id, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) AS total_amount FROM accounts r LEFT JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY r.account_id ORDER BY r.account_id;

business_scenario: Find accounts whose total event amount exceeds 20000.
solution_approach: I will join accounts and transactions and group by account id to sum event amounts. I will use HAVING to keep totals above 20000.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.account_id, SUM(e.amount) AS total_amount FROM accounts r JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY r.account_id HAVING SUM(e.amount)>20000 ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Count accounts by customers segment.
solution_approach: I will link accounts to customers by customer id. I will group by segment and count the matching accounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment, COUNT(r.account_id) AS record_count FROM customers m LEFT JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.segment ORDER BY m.segment;

business_scenario: Calculate average balance by account products category.
solution_approach: I will join account products and accounts by product id. I will group by category and average balance.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category, AVG(r.balance) AS average_amount FROM account_products c JOIN accounts r ON c.product_id=r.product_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Show customers, accounts and account products names together.
solution_approach: I will join customers, accounts and account products through customer id and product id to show customer name, product name, and status.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_name, r.account_id, c.product_name, r.status FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id JOIN account_products c ON r.product_id=c.product_id ORDER BY r.account_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total balance for each customers.
solution_approach: I will join customers and accounts and sum balance for each customers.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,SUM(r.balance) AS total_amount FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find accounts whose balance is above the overall average.
solution_approach: I will compare each balance in accounts with the overall average from a subquery.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT account_id,balance FROM accounts WHERE balance>(SELECT AVG(balance) FROM accounts) ORDER BY balance DESC;

business_scenario: Show transactions with their parent accounts status.
solution_approach: I will join transactions to accounts using the parent key.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT e.transaction_id,e.transaction_date,e.transaction_type,e.amount,r.status AS record_status FROM transactions e JOIN accounts r ON e.account_id=r.account_id ORDER BY e.transaction_id;

business_scenario: Calculate completed and failed event amounts for every accounts.
solution_approach: I will join accounts and transactions and use CASE inside SUM for Completed and Failed event amounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.account_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM accounts r LEFT JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY r.account_id ORDER BY r.account_id;

business_scenario: Count transactions by calendar month.
solution_approach: I will derive the month from transaction date, group transactions and count each month.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',transaction_date)::date AS event_month,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM transactions GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',transaction_date) ORDER BY event_month;

business_scenario: Find customers with no accounts.
solution_approach: I will left join accounts to customers on customer id and keep customers with no accounts key.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name FROM customers m LEFT JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id WHERE r.account_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Find account products items that are unused by accounts.
solution_approach: I will left join accounts to account products on product id and keep account products with no matching accounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.product_id,c.product_name FROM account_products c LEFT JOIN accounts r ON c.product_id=r.product_id WHERE r.account_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.product_id;

business_scenario: Find the earliest accounts date for every customers.
solution_approach: I will join customers and accounts, group by customer id and take the minimum open date.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,MIN(r.open_date) AS first_date FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Find the latest transactions date for every accounts.
solution_approach: I will left join transactions to accounts, group by account id and take the maximum transaction date.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.account_id,MAX(e.transaction_date) AS latest_event_date FROM accounts r LEFT JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY r.account_id ORDER BY r.account_id;

business_scenario: List distinct customers with at least one completed transactions.
solution_approach: I will join customers, accounts and transactions, keep Completed events and remove duplicate customers.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.customer_id,m.customer_name FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id WHERE e.status='Completed' ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Calculate average event amount by account products category.
solution_approach: I will join account products, accounts and transactions through their keys. I will group by category and average event amount.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category,AVG(e.amount) AS average_event_amount FROM account_products c JOIN accounts r ON c.product_id=r.product_id JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Count accounts by master segment and record status.
solution_approach: I will join customers and accounts and group counts by segment and status.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment,r.status,COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.segment,r.status ORDER BY m.segment,r.status;

business_scenario: Rank customers by total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join customers, accounts and transactions and total event amounts per customers. I will rank the totals from highest to lowest.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,SUM(e.amount) total_amount FROM customers m JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,total_amount,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM totals ORDER BY amount_rank,customer_id;

business_scenario: Find accounts whose latest event was before 1 January 2026 or is missing.
solution_approach: I will left join transactions to accounts using account id so accounts without activity remain. I will group each accounts by account id and use HAVING on its latest transaction date.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.account_id,MAX(e.transaction_date) AS latest_event_date FROM accounts r LEFT JOIN transactions e ON r.account_id=e.account_id GROUP BY r.account_id HAVING MAX(e.transaction_date)<DATE '2026-01-01' OR MAX(e.transaction_date) IS NULL ORDER BY r.account_id;

business_scenario: Find customers whose total balance is above the average master total.
solution_approach: I will use a CTE to total balance by customer id in accounts. I will keep customers totals above the average total.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT customer_id,SUM(balance) total_amount FROM accounts GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id,total_amount FROM totals WHERE total_amount>(SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM totals) ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Classify accounts into High, Medium and Low amount bands.
solution_approach: I will classify accounts using CASE with 100000 and 50000 balance boundaries.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT account_id,balance,CASE WHEN balance>=100000 THEN 'High' WHEN balance>=50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END amount_band FROM accounts ORDER BY account_id;

business_scenario: Show month-over-month event amount for every accounts.
solution_approach: I will total event amounts in transactions by account id and month in a CTE. I will use LAG partitioned by account id and ordered by event month.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); account_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); accounts(account_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, open_date, status, balance); transactions(transaction_id PK, account_id FK, transaction_date, transaction_type, quantity, amount, status)

business_scenario: Show patients, appointments and doctors names together.

schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.patient_name, r.appointment_id, c.doctor_name, r.status FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id JOIN doctors c ON r.doctor_id=c.doctor_id ORDER BY r.appointment_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total bill_amount for each patients.
solution_approach: I will join patients and appointments and sum bill amount for each patients.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name,SUM(r.bill_amount) AS total_amount FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id GROUP BY m.patient_id,m.patient_name ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find appointments whose bill_amount is above the overall average.
solution_approach: I will compare each bill amount in appointments with the overall average from a subquery.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT appointment_id,bill_amount FROM appointments WHERE bill_amount>(SELECT AVG(bill_amount) FROM appointments) ORDER BY bill_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Show visits with their parent appointments status.
solution_approach: I will join visits to appointments using the parent key.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT e.visit_id,e.visit_date,e.visit_type,e.amount,r.status AS record_status FROM visits e JOIN appointments r ON e.appointment_id=r.appointment_id ORDER BY e.visit_id;

business_scenario: Calculate completed and failed event amounts for every appointments.
solution_approach: I will join appointments and visits and use CASE inside SUM for Completed and Failed event amounts.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.appointment_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM appointments r LEFT JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY r.appointment_id ORDER BY r.appointment_id;

business_scenario: Count visits by calendar month.
solution_approach: I will derive the month from visit date, group visits and count each month.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',visit_date)::date AS event_month,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM visits GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',visit_date) ORDER BY event_month;

business_scenario: Find patients with no appointments.
solution_approach: I will left join appointments to patients on patient id and keep patients with no appointments key.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name FROM patients m LEFT JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id WHERE r.appointment_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.patient_id;

business_scenario: Find doctors items that are unused by appointments.
solution_approach: I will left join appointments to doctors on doctor id and keep doctors with no matching appointments.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.doctor_id,c.doctor_name FROM doctors c LEFT JOIN appointments r ON c.doctor_id=r.doctor_id WHERE r.appointment_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.doctor_id;

business_scenario: Find the earliest appointments date for every patients.
solution_approach: I will join patients and appointments, group by patient id and take the minimum appointment date.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name,MIN(r.appointment_date) AS first_date FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id GROUP BY m.patient_id,m.patient_name ORDER BY m.patient_id;

business_scenario: Find the latest visits date for every appointments.
solution_approach: I will left join visits to appointments, group by appointment id and take the maximum visit date.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.appointment_id,MAX(e.visit_date) AS latest_event_date FROM appointments r LEFT JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY r.appointment_id ORDER BY r.appointment_id;

business_scenario: List distinct patients with at least one completed visits.
solution_approach: I will join patients, appointments and visits, keep Completed events and remove duplicate patients.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id,m.patient_name FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id WHERE e.status='Completed' ORDER BY m.patient_id;

business_scenario: Calculate average event amount by doctors category.
solution_approach: I will join doctors, appointments and visits through their keys. I will group by category and average event amount.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category,AVG(e.amount) AS average_event_amount FROM doctors c JOIN appointments r ON c.doctor_id=r.doctor_id JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Count appointments by master segment and record status.
solution_approach: I will join patients and appointments and group counts by segment and status.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment,r.status,COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id GROUP BY m.segment,r.status ORDER BY m.segment,r.status;

business_scenario: Rank patients by total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join patients, appointments and visits and total event amounts per patients. I will rank the totals from highest to lowest.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name,SUM(e.amount) total_amount FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY m.patient_id,m.patient_name) SELECT patient_id,patient_name,total_amount,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM totals ORDER BY amount_rank,patient_id;

business_scenario: Find appointments whose latest event was before 1 January 2026 or is missing.
solution_approach: I will left join visits to appointments using appointment id so appointments without activity remain. I will group each appointments by appointment id and use HAVING on its latest visit date.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.appointment_id,MAX(e.visit_date) AS latest_event_date FROM appointments r LEFT JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY r.appointment_id HAVING MAX(e.visit_date)<DATE '2026-01-01' OR MAX(e.visit_date) IS NULL ORDER BY r.appointment_id;

business_scenario: Find patients whose total bill_amount is above the average master total.
solution_approach: I will use a CTE to total bill amount by patient id in appointments. I will keep patients totals above the average total.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT patient_id,SUM(bill_amount) total_amount FROM appointments GROUP BY patient_id) SELECT patient_id,total_amount FROM totals WHERE total_amount>(SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM totals) ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Classify appointments into High, Medium and Low amount bands.
solution_approach: I will classify appointments using CASE with 100000 and 50000 bill amount boundaries.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT appointment_id,bill_amount,CASE WHEN bill_amount>=100000 THEN 'High' WHEN bill_amount>=50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END amount_band FROM appointments ORDER BY appointment_id;

business_scenario: Show month-over-month event amount for every appointments.
solution_approach: I will total event amounts in visits by appointment id and month in a CTE. I will use LAG partitioned by appointment id and ordered by event month.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT appointment_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',visit_date)::date event_month,SUM(amount) monthly_amount FROM visits GROUP BY appointment_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',visit_date)) SELECT appointment_id,event_month,monthly_amount,LAG(monthly_amount) OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id ORDER BY event_month) previous_month_amount FROM monthly ORDER BY appointment_id,event_month;

business_scenario: Calculate a running event total within every appointments.
solution_approach: I will use a windowed SUM of amount in visits partitioned by appointment id and ordered by visit date and visit id.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT appointment_id,visit_id,visit_date,amount,SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id ORDER BY visit_date,visit_id) running_amount FROM visits ORDER BY appointment_id,visit_date,visit_id;

business_scenario: Return the two largest visits for every appointment id.
solution_approach: I will assign row numbers within each appointment id in visits by descending amount. I will keep row numbers 1 and 2 for every appointment id.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id ORDER BY amount DESC,visit_id) rn FROM visits e) SELECT visit_id,appointment_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY appointment_id,rn;

business_scenario: Calculate each appointments share of total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join appointments and visits to total amounts for each appointments in a CTE. I will divide each appointments total by the windowed grand total.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT r.appointment_id,COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) total_amount FROM appointments r LEFT JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY r.appointment_id) SELECT appointment_id,total_amount,ROUND(100.0*total_amount/NULLIF(SUM(total_amount) OVER(),0),2) percent_of_total FROM totals ORDER BY appointment_id;

business_scenario: Dense-rank appointments by bill_amount within each patients.
solution_approach: I will dense rank appointments within each patient id by descending bill amount.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT patient_id,appointment_id,bill_amount,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY bill_amount DESC) amount_rank FROM appointments ORDER BY patient_id,amount_rank,appointment_id;

business_scenario: Show each event amount beside the previous event amount.
solution_approach: I will use LAG in visits partitioned by appointment id ordered by visit date and visit id.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT appointment_id,visit_id,visit_date,amount,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id ORDER BY visit_date,visit_id) previous_amount FROM visits ORDER BY appointment_id,visit_date,visit_id;

business_scenario: Calculate a three-event moving average for each appointments.
solution_approach: I will average the current and two preceding amounts in visits partitioned by appointment id ordered by visit date and visit id.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT appointment_id,visit_id,visit_date,amount,AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id ORDER BY visit_date,visit_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) moving_average FROM visits ORDER BY appointment_id,visit_date,visit_id;

business_scenario: Find patients whose every appointments is Active.
solution_approach: I will use EXISTS to require that each patients has at least one appointments. I will use NOT EXISTS to exclude patients with a non-Active appointments.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name FROM patients m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM appointments r WHERE r.patient_id=m.patient_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM appointments r WHERE r.patient_id=m.patient_id AND r.status<>'Active') ORDER BY m.patient_id;

business_scenario: Find appointments above the average bill_amount for their status.
solution_approach: I will compare each appointments with the average bill amount for its own status.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT appointment_id,status,bill_amount FROM appointments r WHERE bill_amount>(SELECT AVG(x.bill_amount) FROM appointments x WHERE x.status=r.status) ORDER BY status,bill_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Calculate days between the first and last event for each appointments.
solution_approach: I will join appointments and visits, group by appointment id and take minimum and maximum visit date. I will subtract the first date from the last date to get active days.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.appointment_id,MIN(e.visit_date) first_event,MAX(e.visit_date) last_event,MAX(e.visit_date)-MIN(e.visit_date) active_days FROM appointments r JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY r.appointment_id ORDER BY r.appointment_id;

business_scenario: Calculate every event's percentage contribution to its appointments total.
solution_approach: I will divide each visits amount by the total amount within its appointment id partition.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT visit_id,appointment_id,amount,ROUND(100.0*amount/NULLIF(SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id),0),2) record_percent FROM visits ORDER BY appointment_id,visit_id;

business_scenario: Return the highest-value patients in each segment.
solution_approach: I will join patients and appointments to total bill amount for every patients and segment. I will row-number within each segment and keep rank 1.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name,m.segment,SUM(r.bill_amount) total_amount FROM patients m JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id GROUP BY m.patient_id,m.patient_name,m.segment), ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total_amount DESC,patient_id) rn FROM totals) SELECT patient_id,patient_name,segment,total_amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY segment;

business_scenario: Find visits whose amount is above their parent record average.
solution_approach: I will compare each visits amount with the average amount for its parent appointment id.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT visit_id,appointment_id,amount FROM visits e WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM visits x WHERE x.appointment_id=e.appointment_id) ORDER BY appointment_id,amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find patients whose record count is above the average master record count.
solution_approach: I will left join patients and appointments and count appointments for every patients in a CTE. I will keep patients counts above the average master count.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.patient_id,m.patient_name,COUNT(r.appointment_id) record_count FROM patients m LEFT JOIN appointments r ON m.patient_id=r.patient_id GROUP BY m.patient_id,m.patient_name) SELECT patient_id,patient_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,patient_id;

business_scenario: Show completed, pending and failed event totals per appointments.
solution_approach: I will join appointments and visits to conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per appointments.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.appointment_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Pending' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) pending_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) failed_amount FROM appointments r LEFT JOIN visits e ON r.appointment_id=e.appointment_id GROUP BY r.appointment_id ORDER BY r.appointment_id;

business_scenario: Return the latest visits row for every appointment id.
solution_approach: I will row number visits partitioned by appointment id from newest to oldest by visit date and visit id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: patients(patient_id PK, patient_name, city, segment, joined_date); doctors(doctor_id PK, doctor_name, category, status, base_value); appointments(appointment_id PK, patient_id FK, doctor_id FK, appointment_date, status, bill_amount); visits(visit_id PK, appointment_id FK, visit_date, visit_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY appointment_id ORDER BY visit_date DESC,visit_id DESC) rn FROM visits e) SELECT visit_id,appointment_id,visit_date,visit_type,amount,status FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY appointment_id;

business_scenario: Retrieve all active insurance policies to confirm current policyholder coverage.
solution_approach: I will keep only policies whose status is Active.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM policies WHERE status = 'Active';

business_scenario: Find high-premium policies with premium amount greater than 50000 for underwriting risk review.
solution_approach: I will filter policies where premium amount is greater than 50000.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)

business_scenario: List policyholder clients based in Chennai to assess regional claim exposure.
solution_approach: I will keep customers whose city is Chennai.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chennai';

business_scenario: Count all insurance policies issued by the underwriting division.
solution_approach: I will count every row in the policies table.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_records FROM policies;

business_scenario: Show insurance policies ordered from highest to lowest premium amount.
solution_approach: I will order policies by premium amount from highest to lowest.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM policies ORDER BY premium_amount DESC;

business_scenario: List distinct insurance plan categories available in the insurance products catalog.
solution_approach: I will return distinct category values from insurance products.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM insurance_products ORDER BY category;

business_scenario: Find insurance policies starting on or after 1 January 2026.
solution_approach: I will filter policies with start date on or after 1 January 2026.

business_scenario: Find insurance claims filed between 1 January and 30 June 2026.
solution_approach: I will filter claims to dates between January and June 2026.

business_scenario: Calculate the average annual premium amount across all issued policies.
solution_approach: I will calculate the average premium amount across all policies.

answer_sql: SELECT AVG(premium_amount) AS average_amount FROM policies;

business_scenario: Find the maximum claim payout amount recorded in claims.
solution_approach: I will use MAX on amount to find the largest event value.

answer_sql: SELECT MAX(amount) AS largest_amount FROM claims;

business_scenario: Count distinct policyholder cities covered across the insurance network.
solution_approach: I will count the distinct city values in customers.
