answer_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) AS city_count FROM customers;

business_scenario: Return resolved claims with status Completed for actuarial loss reporting.
solution_approach: I will keep claims whose status is Completed.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM claims WHERE status = 'Completed';

business_scenario: Classify insurance policies into High, Medium, or Low premium tiers using premium amount.
solution_approach: I will use CASE on premium amount with 100000 and 50000 boundaries.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id, premium_amount, CASE WHEN premium_amount >= 100000 THEN 'High' WHEN premium_amount >= 50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS amount_band FROM policies ORDER BY policy_id;

business_scenario: Find Active insurance policies with a premium of at least 50000 for reinsurer treaty reporting.
solution_approach: I will require Active status and premium amount of at least 50000.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM policies WHERE status = 'Active' AND premium_amount >= 50000;

business_scenario: Show each customers name with its policies details.
solution_approach: I will join customers to policies using customer id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_name, r.policy_id, r.status, r.premium_amount FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id ORDER BY m.customer_id,r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Count policies for every insurance products item.
solution_approach: I will left join insurance products to policies by product id. I will group each insurance products item and count matching policies.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.product_name, COUNT(r.policy_id) AS record_count FROM insurance_products c LEFT JOIN policies r ON c.product_id=r.product_id GROUP BY c.product_id,c.product_name ORDER BY c.product_id;

business_scenario: Find policies that have no claims.
solution_approach: I will left join claims to policies on policy id and keep policies with a null claim id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id WHERE e.claim_id IS NULL ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total event amount for each policies.
solution_approach: I will join policies to claims using policy id. I will group by policy id and sum event amounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) AS total_amount FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Find policies whose total event amount exceeds 20000.
solution_approach: I will join policies and claims and group by policy id to sum event amounts. I will use HAVING to keep totals above 20000.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id, SUM(e.amount) AS total_amount FROM policies r JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id HAVING SUM(e.amount)>20000 ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Count policies by customers segment.
solution_approach: I will link policies to customers by customer id. I will group by segment and count the matching policies.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment, COUNT(r.policy_id) AS record_count FROM customers m LEFT JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.segment ORDER BY m.segment;

business_scenario: Calculate average premium_amount by insurance products category.
solution_approach: I will join insurance products and policies by product id. I will group by category and average premium amount.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category, AVG(r.premium_amount) AS average_amount FROM insurance_products c JOIN policies r ON c.product_id=r.product_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Show customers, policies and insurance products names together.
solution_approach: I will join customers, policies and insurance products through customer id and product id to show customer name, product name, and status.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_name, r.policy_id, c.product_name, r.status FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id JOIN insurance_products c ON r.product_id=c.product_id ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total premium_amount for each customers.
solution_approach: I will join customers and policies and sum premium amount for each customers.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,SUM(r.premium_amount) AS total_amount FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find policies whose premium_amount is above the overall average.
solution_approach: I will compare each premium amount in policies with the overall average from a subquery.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id,premium_amount FROM policies WHERE premium_amount>(SELECT AVG(premium_amount) FROM policies) ORDER BY premium_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Show claims with their parent policies status.
solution_approach: I will join claims to policies using the parent key.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT e.claim_id,e.claim_date,e.claim_type,e.amount,r.status AS record_status FROM claims e JOIN policies r ON e.policy_id=r.policy_id ORDER BY e.claim_id;

business_scenario: Calculate completed and failed event amounts for every policies.
solution_approach: I will join policies and claims and use CASE inside SUM for Completed and Failed event amounts.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Count claims by calendar month.
solution_approach: I will derive the month from claim date, group claims and count each month.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',claim_date)::date AS event_month,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM claims GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',claim_date) ORDER BY event_month;

business_scenario: Find customers with no policies.
solution_approach: I will left join policies to customers on customer id and keep customers with no policies key.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name FROM customers m LEFT JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id WHERE r.policy_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Find insurance products items that are unused by policies.
solution_approach: I will left join policies to insurance products on product id and keep insurance products with no matching policies.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.product_id,c.product_name FROM insurance_products c LEFT JOIN policies r ON c.product_id=r.product_id WHERE r.policy_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.product_id;

business_scenario: Find the earliest policies date for every customers.
solution_approach: I will join customers and policies, group by customer id and take the minimum start date.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,MIN(r.start_date) AS first_date FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Find the latest claims date for every policies.
solution_approach: I will left join claims to policies, group by policy id and take the maximum claim date.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id,MAX(e.claim_date) AS latest_event_date FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: List distinct customers with at least one completed claims.
solution_approach: I will join customers, policies and claims, keep Completed events and remove duplicate customers.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.customer_id,m.customer_name FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id WHERE e.status='Completed' ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Calculate average event amount by insurance products category.
solution_approach: I will join insurance products, policies and claims through their keys. I will group by category and average event amount.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category,AVG(e.amount) AS average_event_amount FROM insurance_products c JOIN policies r ON c.product_id=r.product_id JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Count policies by master segment and record status.
solution_approach: I will join customers and policies and group counts by segment and status.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment,r.status,COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.segment,r.status ORDER BY m.segment,r.status;

business_scenario: Rank customers by total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join customers, policies and claims and total event amounts per customers. I will rank the totals from highest to lowest.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,SUM(e.amount) total_amount FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,total_amount,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM totals ORDER BY amount_rank,customer_id;

business_scenario: Find policies whose latest event was before 1 January 2026 or is missing.
solution_approach: I will left join claims to policies using policy id so policies without activity remain. I will group each policies by policy id and use HAVING on its latest claim date.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id,MAX(e.claim_date) AS latest_event_date FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id HAVING MAX(e.claim_date)<DATE '2026-01-01' OR MAX(e.claim_date) IS NULL ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Find customers whose total premium_amount is above the average master total.
solution_approach: I will use a CTE to total premium amount by customer id in policies. I will keep customers totals above the average total.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT customer_id,SUM(premium_amount) total_amount FROM policies GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id,total_amount FROM totals WHERE total_amount>(SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM totals) ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Classify policies into High, Medium and Low amount bands.
solution_approach: I will classify policies using CASE with 100000 and 50000 premium amount boundaries.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id,premium_amount,CASE WHEN premium_amount>=100000 THEN 'High' WHEN premium_amount>=50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END amount_band FROM policies ORDER BY policy_id;

business_scenario: Show month-over-month event amount for every policies.
solution_approach: I will total event amounts in claims by policy id and month in a CTE. I will use LAG partitioned by policy id and ordered by event month.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT policy_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',claim_date)::date event_month,SUM(amount) monthly_amount FROM claims GROUP BY policy_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',claim_date)) SELECT policy_id,event_month,monthly_amount,LAG(monthly_amount) OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY event_month) previous_month_amount FROM monthly ORDER BY policy_id,event_month;

business_scenario: Calculate a running event total within every policies.
solution_approach: I will use a windowed SUM of amount in claims partitioned by policy id and ordered by claim date and claim id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id,claim_id,claim_date,amount,SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY claim_date,claim_id) running_amount FROM claims ORDER BY policy_id,claim_date,claim_id;

business_scenario: Return the two largest claims for every policy id.
solution_approach: I will assign row numbers within each policy id in claims by descending amount. I will keep row numbers 1 and 2 for every policy id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY amount DESC,claim_id) rn FROM claims e) SELECT claim_id,policy_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY policy_id,rn;

business_scenario: Calculate each policies share of total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join policies and claims to total amounts for each policies in a CTE. I will divide each policies total by the windowed grand total.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT r.policy_id,COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) total_amount FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id) SELECT policy_id,total_amount,ROUND(100.0*total_amount/NULLIF(SUM(total_amount) OVER(),0),2) percent_of_total FROM totals ORDER BY policy_id;

business_scenario: Dense-rank policies by premium_amount within each customers.
solution_approach: I will dense rank policies within each customer id by descending premium amount.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT customer_id,policy_id,premium_amount,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY premium_amount DESC) amount_rank FROM policies ORDER BY customer_id,amount_rank,policy_id;

business_scenario: Show each event amount beside the previous event amount.
solution_approach: I will use LAG in claims partitioned by policy id ordered by claim date and claim id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id,claim_id,claim_date,amount,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY claim_date,claim_id) previous_amount FROM claims ORDER BY policy_id,claim_date,claim_id;

business_scenario: Calculate a three-event moving average for each policies.
solution_approach: I will average the current and two preceding amounts in claims partitioned by policy id ordered by claim date and claim id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id,claim_id,claim_date,amount,AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY claim_date,claim_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) moving_average FROM claims ORDER BY policy_id,claim_date,claim_id;

business_scenario: Find customers whose every policies is Active.
solution_approach: I will use EXISTS to require that each customers has at least one policies. I will use NOT EXISTS to exclude customers with a non-Active policies.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name FROM customers m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM policies r WHERE r.customer_id=m.customer_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM policies r WHERE r.customer_id=m.customer_id AND r.status<>'Active') ORDER BY m.customer_id;

business_scenario: Find policies above the average premium_amount for their status.
solution_approach: I will compare each policies with the average premium amount for its own status.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT policy_id,status,premium_amount FROM policies r WHERE premium_amount>(SELECT AVG(x.premium_amount) FROM policies x WHERE x.status=r.status) ORDER BY status,premium_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Calculate days between the first and last event for each policies.
solution_approach: I will join policies and claims, group by policy id and take minimum and maximum claim date. I will subtract the first date from the last date to get active days.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id,MIN(e.claim_date) first_event,MAX(e.claim_date) last_event,MAX(e.claim_date)-MIN(e.claim_date) active_days FROM policies r JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Calculate every event's percentage contribution to its policies total.
solution_approach: I will divide each claims amount by the total amount within its policy id partition.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT claim_id,policy_id,amount,ROUND(100.0*amount/NULLIF(SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id),0),2) record_percent FROM claims ORDER BY policy_id,claim_id;

business_scenario: Return the highest-value customers in each segment.
solution_approach: I will join customers and policies to total premium amount for every customers and segment. I will row-number within each segment and keep rank 1.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,m.segment,SUM(r.premium_amount) total_amount FROM customers m JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name,m.segment), ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total_amount DESC,customer_id) rn FROM totals) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,segment,total_amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY segment;

business_scenario: Find claims whose amount is above their parent record average.
solution_approach: I will compare each claims amount with the average amount for its parent policy id.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT claim_id,policy_id,amount FROM claims e WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM claims x WHERE x.policy_id=e.policy_id) ORDER BY policy_id,amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find customers whose record count is above the average master record count.
solution_approach: I will left join customers and policies and count policies for every customers in a CTE. I will keep customers counts above the average master count.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,COUNT(r.policy_id) record_count FROM customers m LEFT JOIN policies r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,customer_id;

business_scenario: Show completed, pending and failed event totals per policies.
solution_approach: I will join policies and claims to conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per policies.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.policy_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Pending' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) pending_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) failed_amount FROM policies r LEFT JOIN claims e ON r.policy_id=e.policy_id GROUP BY r.policy_id ORDER BY r.policy_id;

business_scenario: Return the latest claims row for every policy id.
solution_approach: I will row number claims partitioned by policy id from newest to oldest by claim date and claim id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY claim_date DESC,claim_id DESC) rn FROM claims e) SELECT claim_id,policy_id,claim_date,claim_type,amount,status FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY policy_id;

solution_approach: I will join holdings and trades and use CASE inside SUM for Completed and Failed event amounts.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.holding_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM holdings r LEFT JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY r.holding_id ORDER BY r.holding_id;

business_scenario: Count trades by calendar month.
solution_approach: I will derive the month from trade date, group trades and count each month.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',trade_date)::date AS event_month,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM trades GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',trade_date) ORDER BY event_month;

business_scenario: Find investors with no holdings.
solution_approach: I will left join holdings to investors on investor id and keep investors with no holdings key.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.investor_id,m.investor_name FROM investors m LEFT JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id WHERE r.holding_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.investor_id;

business_scenario: Find securities items that are unused by holdings.
solution_approach: I will left join holdings to securities on security id and keep securities with no matching holdings.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.security_id,c.security_name FROM securities c LEFT JOIN holdings r ON c.security_id=r.security_id WHERE r.holding_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.security_id;

business_scenario: Find the earliest holdings date for every investors.
solution_approach: I will join investors and holdings, group by investor id and take the minimum acquired date.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.investor_id,m.investor_name,MIN(r.acquired_date) AS first_date FROM investors m JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id GROUP BY m.investor_id,m.investor_name ORDER BY m.investor_id;

business_scenario: Find the latest trades date for every holdings.
solution_approach: I will left join trades to holdings, group by holding id and take the maximum trade date.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.holding_id,MAX(e.trade_date) AS latest_event_date FROM holdings r LEFT JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY r.holding_id ORDER BY r.holding_id;

business_scenario: List distinct investors with at least one completed trades.
solution_approach: I will join investors, holdings and trades, keep Completed events and remove duplicate investors.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.investor_id,m.investor_name FROM investors m JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id WHERE e.status='Completed' ORDER BY m.investor_id;

business_scenario: Calculate average event amount by securities category.
solution_approach: I will join securities, holdings and trades through their keys. I will group by category and average event amount.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category,AVG(e.amount) AS average_event_amount FROM securities c JOIN holdings r ON c.security_id=r.security_id JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Count holdings by master segment and record status.
solution_approach: I will join investors and holdings and group counts by segment and status.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment,r.status,COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM investors m JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id GROUP BY m.segment,r.status ORDER BY m.segment,r.status;

business_scenario: Rank investors by total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join investors, holdings and trades and total event amounts per investors. I will rank the totals from highest to lowest.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.investor_id,m.investor_name,SUM(e.amount) total_amount FROM investors m JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY m.investor_id,m.investor_name) SELECT investor_id,investor_name,total_amount,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM totals ORDER BY amount_rank,investor_id;

business_scenario: Find holdings whose latest event was before 1 January 2026 or is missing.
solution_approach: I will left join trades to holdings using holding id so holdings without activity remain. I will group each holdings by holding id and use HAVING on its latest trade date.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.holding_id,MAX(e.trade_date) AS latest_event_date FROM holdings r LEFT JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY r.holding_id HAVING MAX(e.trade_date)<DATE '2026-01-01' OR MAX(e.trade_date) IS NULL ORDER BY r.holding_id;

business_scenario: Find investors whose total market_value is above the average master total.
solution_approach: I will use a CTE to total market value by investor id in holdings. I will keep investors totals above the average total.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT investor_id,SUM(market_value) total_amount FROM holdings GROUP BY investor_id) SELECT investor_id,total_amount FROM totals WHERE total_amount>(SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM totals) ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Classify holdings into High, Medium and Low amount bands.
solution_approach: I will classify holdings using CASE with 100000 and 50000 market value boundaries.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT holding_id,market_value,CASE WHEN market_value>=100000 THEN 'High' WHEN market_value>=50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END amount_band FROM holdings ORDER BY holding_id;

business_scenario: Show month-over-month event amount for every holdings.
solution_approach: I will total event amounts in trades by holding id and month in a CTE. I will use LAG partitioned by holding id and ordered by event month.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT holding_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',trade_date)::date event_month,SUM(amount) monthly_amount FROM trades GROUP BY holding_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',trade_date)) SELECT holding_id,event_month,monthly_amount,LAG(monthly_amount) OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id ORDER BY event_month) previous_month_amount FROM monthly ORDER BY holding_id,event_month;

business_scenario: Calculate a running event total within every holdings.
solution_approach: I will use a windowed SUM of amount in trades partitioned by holding id and ordered by trade date and trade id.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT holding_id,trade_id,trade_date,amount,SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id ORDER BY trade_date,trade_id) running_amount FROM trades ORDER BY holding_id,trade_date,trade_id;

business_scenario: Return the two largest trades for every holding id.
solution_approach: I will assign row numbers within each holding id in trades by descending amount. I will keep row numbers 1 and 2 for every holding id.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id ORDER BY amount DESC,trade_id) rn FROM trades e) SELECT trade_id,holding_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY holding_id,rn;

business_scenario: Calculate each holdings share of total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join holdings and trades to total amounts for each holdings in a CTE. I will divide each holdings total by the windowed grand total.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT r.holding_id,COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) total_amount FROM holdings r LEFT JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY r.holding_id) SELECT holding_id,total_amount,ROUND(100.0*total_amount/NULLIF(SUM(total_amount) OVER(),0),2) percent_of_total FROM totals ORDER BY holding_id;

business_scenario: Dense-rank holdings by market_value within each investors.
solution_approach: I will dense rank holdings within each investor id by descending market value.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT investor_id,holding_id,market_value,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY investor_id ORDER BY market_value DESC) amount_rank FROM holdings ORDER BY investor_id,amount_rank,holding_id;

business_scenario: Show each event amount beside the previous event amount.
solution_approach: I will use LAG in trades partitioned by holding id ordered by trade date and trade id.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT holding_id,trade_id,trade_date,amount,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id ORDER BY trade_date,trade_id) previous_amount FROM trades ORDER BY holding_id,trade_date,trade_id;

business_scenario: Calculate a three-event moving average for each holdings.
solution_approach: I will average the current and two preceding amounts in trades partitioned by holding id ordered by trade date and trade id.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT holding_id,trade_id,trade_date,amount,AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id ORDER BY trade_date,trade_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) moving_average FROM trades ORDER BY holding_id,trade_date,trade_id;

business_scenario: Find investors whose every holdings is Active.
solution_approach: I will use EXISTS to require that each investors has at least one holdings. I will use NOT EXISTS to exclude investors with a non-Active holdings.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.investor_id,m.investor_name FROM investors m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM holdings r WHERE r.investor_id=m.investor_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM holdings r WHERE r.investor_id=m.investor_id AND r.status<>'Active') ORDER BY m.investor_id;

business_scenario: Find holdings above the average market_value for their status.
solution_approach: I will compare each holdings with the average market value for its own status.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT holding_id,status,market_value FROM holdings r WHERE market_value>(SELECT AVG(x.market_value) FROM holdings x WHERE x.status=r.status) ORDER BY status,market_value DESC;

business_scenario: Calculate days between the first and last event for each holdings.
solution_approach: I will join holdings and trades, group by holding id and take minimum and maximum trade date. I will subtract the first date from the last date to get active days.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.holding_id,MIN(e.trade_date) first_event,MAX(e.trade_date) last_event,MAX(e.trade_date)-MIN(e.trade_date) active_days FROM holdings r JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY r.holding_id ORDER BY r.holding_id;

business_scenario: Calculate every event's percentage contribution to its holdings total.
solution_approach: I will divide each trades amount by the total amount within its holding id partition.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT trade_id,holding_id,amount,ROUND(100.0*amount/NULLIF(SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id),0),2) record_percent FROM trades ORDER BY holding_id,trade_id;

business_scenario: Return the highest-value investors in each segment.
solution_approach: I will join investors and holdings to total market value for every investors and segment. I will row-number within each segment and keep rank 1.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.investor_id,m.investor_name,m.segment,SUM(r.market_value) total_amount FROM investors m JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id GROUP BY m.investor_id,m.investor_name,m.segment), ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total_amount DESC,investor_id) rn FROM totals) SELECT investor_id,investor_name,segment,total_amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY segment;

business_scenario: Find trades whose amount is above their parent record average.
solution_approach: I will compare each trades amount with the average amount for its parent holding id.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT trade_id,holding_id,amount FROM trades e WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM trades x WHERE x.holding_id=e.holding_id) ORDER BY holding_id,amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find investors whose record count is above the average master record count.
solution_approach: I will left join investors and holdings and count holdings for every investors in a CTE. I will keep investors counts above the average master count.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.investor_id,m.investor_name,COUNT(r.holding_id) record_count FROM investors m LEFT JOIN holdings r ON m.investor_id=r.investor_id GROUP BY m.investor_id,m.investor_name) SELECT investor_id,investor_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,investor_id;

business_scenario: Show completed, pending and failed event totals per holdings.
solution_approach: I will join holdings and trades to conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per holdings.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.holding_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Pending' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) pending_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) failed_amount FROM holdings r LEFT JOIN trades e ON r.holding_id=e.holding_id GROUP BY r.holding_id ORDER BY r.holding_id;

business_scenario: Return the latest trades row for every holding id.
solution_approach: I will row number trades partitioned by holding id from newest to oldest by trade date and trade id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: investors(investor_id PK, investor_name, city, segment, joined_date); securities(security_id PK, security_name, category, status, base_value); holdings(holding_id PK, investor_id FK, security_id FK, acquired_date, status, market_value); trades(trade_id PK, holding_id FK, trade_date, trade_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY holding_id ORDER BY trade_date DESC,trade_id DESC) rn FROM trades e) SELECT trade_id,holding_id,trade_date,trade_type,amount,status FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY holding_id;

business_scenario: List distinct chip architecture categories available in the chip products catalog.

solution_approach: I will order by client id and limit the result to five rows.

business_scenario: Find production batches with manufacturing costs between 25000 and 75000 for standard run auditing.
solution_approach: I will keep production batches whose batch cost is between 25000 and 75000.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)

business_scenario: Find client tech firms whose name starts with A for supplier contract review.
solution_approach: I will use a prefix match to keep clients names starting with A.

answer_sql: SELECT * FROM production_batches WHERE status IN ('Active','Pending');

business_scenario: List semiconductor clients in the Premium tier receiving dedicated fab capacity.
solution_approach: I will filter clients to the Premium segment only.

business_scenario: Find wafer test inspections conducted between 1 January and 30 June 2026.
solution_approach: I will filter test results to dates between January and June 2026.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM test_results WHERE test_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-06-30';

business_scenario: Calculate the average production batch cost across all wafer lots.
solution_approach: I will calculate the average batch cost across all production batches.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
