business_scenario: Find the maximum test measurement or cost amount recorded in test results.
solution_approach: I will use MAX on amount to find the largest event value.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT MAX(amount) AS largest_amount FROM test_results;

business_scenario: Count distinct client manufacturing hub cities represented in the client directory.
solution_approach: I will count the distinct city values in clients.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) AS city_count FROM clients;

business_scenario: Return passed test inspections with status Completed for quality assurance release.
solution_approach: I will keep test results whose status is Completed.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM test_results WHERE status = 'Completed';

business_scenario: Classify fabrication batches into High, Medium, or Low cost brackets using batch cost.
solution_approach: I will use CASE on batch cost with 100000 and 50000 boundaries.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id, batch_cost, CASE WHEN batch_cost >= 100000 THEN 'High' WHEN batch_cost >= 50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS amount_band FROM production_batches ORDER BY batch_id;

business_scenario: Find Active production batches with a cost of at least 50000 for cleanroom priority expediting.
solution_approach: I will require Active status and batch cost of at least 50000.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM production_batches WHERE status = 'Active' AND batch_cost >= 50000;

business_scenario: Show each clients name with its production batches details.
solution_approach: I will join clients to production batches using client id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.client_name, r.batch_id, r.status, r.batch_cost FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id ORDER BY m.client_id,r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Count production batches for every chip products item.
solution_approach: I will left join chip products to production batches by product id. I will group each chip products item and count matching production batches.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.product_name, COUNT(r.batch_id) AS record_count FROM chip_products c LEFT JOIN production_batches r ON c.product_id=r.product_id GROUP BY c.product_id,c.product_name ORDER BY c.product_id;

business_scenario: Find production batches that have no test results.
solution_approach: I will left join test results to production batches on batch id and keep production batches with a null test id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id WHERE e.test_id IS NULL ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total event amount for each production batches.
solution_approach: I will join production batches to test results using batch id. I will group by batch id and sum event amounts.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id, COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) AS total_amount FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Find production batches whose total event amount exceeds 20000.
solution_approach: I will join production batches and test results and group by batch id to sum event amounts. I will use HAVING to keep totals above 20000.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id, SUM(e.amount) AS total_amount FROM production_batches r JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id HAVING SUM(e.amount)>20000 ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Count production batches by clients segment.
solution_approach: I will link production batches to clients by client id. I will group by segment and count the matching production batches.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment, COUNT(r.batch_id) AS record_count FROM clients m LEFT JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id GROUP BY m.segment ORDER BY m.segment;

business_scenario: Calculate average batch_cost by chip products category.
solution_approach: I will join chip products and production batches by product id. I will group by category and average batch cost.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category, AVG(r.batch_cost) AS average_amount FROM chip_products c JOIN production_batches r ON c.product_id=r.product_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Show clients, production batches and chip products names together.
solution_approach: I will join clients, production batches and chip products through client id and product id to show client name, product name, and status.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.client_name, r.batch_id, c.product_name, r.status FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id JOIN chip_products c ON r.product_id=c.product_id ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Calculate total batch_cost for each clients.
solution_approach: I will join clients and production batches and sum batch cost for each clients.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name,SUM(r.batch_cost) AS total_amount FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id GROUP BY m.client_id,m.client_name ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find production batches whose batch_cost is above the overall average.
solution_approach: I will compare each batch cost in production batches with the overall average from a subquery.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id,batch_cost FROM production_batches WHERE batch_cost>(SELECT AVG(batch_cost) FROM production_batches) ORDER BY batch_cost DESC;

business_scenario: Show test results with their parent production batches status.
solution_approach: I will join test results to production batches using the parent key.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT e.test_id,e.test_date,e.test_type,e.amount,r.status AS record_status FROM test_results e JOIN production_batches r ON e.batch_id=r.batch_id ORDER BY e.test_id;

business_scenario: Calculate completed and failed event amounts for every production batches.
solution_approach: I will join production batches and test results and use CASE inside SUM for Completed and Failed event amounts.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Count test results by calendar month.
solution_approach: I will derive the month from test date, group test results and count each month.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',test_date)::date AS event_month,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM test_results GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',test_date) ORDER BY event_month;

business_scenario: Find clients with no production batches.
solution_approach: I will left join production batches to clients on client id and keep clients with no production batches key.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name FROM clients m LEFT JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id WHERE r.batch_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.client_id;

business_scenario: Find chip products items that are unused by production batches.
solution_approach: I will left join production batches to chip products on product id and keep chip products with no matching production batches.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.product_id,c.product_name FROM chip_products c LEFT JOIN production_batches r ON c.product_id=r.product_id WHERE r.batch_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.product_id;

business_scenario: Find the earliest production batches date for every clients.
solution_approach: I will join clients and production batches, group by client id and take the minimum production date.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name,MIN(r.production_date) AS first_date FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id GROUP BY m.client_id,m.client_name ORDER BY m.client_id;

business_scenario: Find the latest test results date for every production batches.
solution_approach: I will left join test results to production batches, group by batch id and take the maximum test date.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id,MAX(e.test_date) AS latest_event_date FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: List distinct clients with at least one completed test results.
solution_approach: I will join clients, production batches and test results, keep Completed events and remove duplicate clients.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.client_id,m.client_name FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id WHERE e.status='Completed' ORDER BY m.client_id;

business_scenario: Calculate average event amount by chip products category.
solution_approach: I will join chip products, production batches and test results through their keys. I will group by category and average event amount.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category,AVG(e.amount) AS average_event_amount FROM chip_products c JOIN production_batches r ON c.product_id=r.product_id JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Count production batches by master segment and record status.
solution_approach: I will join clients and production batches and group counts by segment and status.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment,r.status,COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id GROUP BY m.segment,r.status ORDER BY m.segment,r.status;

business_scenario: Rank clients by total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join clients, production batches and test results and total event amounts per clients. I will rank the totals from highest to lowest.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name,SUM(e.amount) total_amount FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY m.client_id,m.client_name) SELECT client_id,client_name,total_amount,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM totals ORDER BY amount_rank,client_id;

business_scenario: Find production batches whose latest event was before 1 January 2026 or is missing.
solution_approach: I will left join test results to production batches using batch id so production batches without activity remain. I will group each production batches by batch id and use HAVING on its latest test date.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id,MAX(e.test_date) AS latest_event_date FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id HAVING MAX(e.test_date)<DATE '2026-01-01' OR MAX(e.test_date) IS NULL ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Find clients whose total batch_cost is above the average master total.
solution_approach: I will use a CTE to total batch cost by client id in production batches. I will keep clients totals above the average total.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT client_id,SUM(batch_cost) total_amount FROM production_batches GROUP BY client_id) SELECT client_id,total_amount FROM totals WHERE total_amount>(SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM totals) ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Classify production batches into High, Medium and Low amount bands.
solution_approach: I will classify production batches using CASE with 100000 and 50000 batch cost boundaries.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id,batch_cost,CASE WHEN batch_cost>=100000 THEN 'High' WHEN batch_cost>=50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END amount_band FROM production_batches ORDER BY batch_id;

business_scenario: Show month-over-month event amount for every production batches.
solution_approach: I will total event amounts in test results by batch id and month in a CTE. I will use LAG partitioned by batch id and ordered by event month.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT batch_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',test_date)::date event_month,SUM(amount) monthly_amount FROM test_results GROUP BY batch_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',test_date)) SELECT batch_id,event_month,monthly_amount,LAG(monthly_amount) OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id ORDER BY event_month) previous_month_amount FROM monthly ORDER BY batch_id,event_month;

business_scenario: Calculate a running event total within every production batches.
solution_approach: I will use a windowed SUM of amount in test results partitioned by batch id and ordered by test date and test id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id,test_id,test_date,amount,SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id ORDER BY test_date,test_id) running_amount FROM test_results ORDER BY batch_id,test_date,test_id;

business_scenario: Return the two largest test results for every batch id.
solution_approach: I will assign row numbers within each batch id in test results by descending amount. I will keep row numbers 1 and 2 for every batch id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id ORDER BY amount DESC,test_id) rn FROM test_results e) SELECT test_id,batch_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY batch_id,rn;

business_scenario: Calculate each production batches share of total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join production batches and test results to total amounts for each production batches in a CTE. I will divide each production batches total by the windowed grand total.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT r.batch_id,COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) total_amount FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id) SELECT batch_id,total_amount,ROUND(100.0*total_amount/NULLIF(SUM(total_amount) OVER(),0),2) percent_of_total FROM totals ORDER BY batch_id;

business_scenario: Dense-rank production batches by batch_cost within each clients.
solution_approach: I will dense rank production batches within each client id by descending batch cost.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT client_id,batch_id,batch_cost,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY client_id ORDER BY batch_cost DESC) amount_rank FROM production_batches ORDER BY client_id,amount_rank,batch_id;

business_scenario: Show each event amount beside the previous event amount.
solution_approach: I will use LAG in test results partitioned by batch id ordered by test date and test id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id,test_id,test_date,amount,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id ORDER BY test_date,test_id) previous_amount FROM test_results ORDER BY batch_id,test_date,test_id;

business_scenario: Calculate a three-event moving average for each production batches.
solution_approach: I will average the current and two preceding amounts in test results partitioned by batch id ordered by test date and test id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id,test_id,test_date,amount,AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id ORDER BY test_date,test_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) moving_average FROM test_results ORDER BY batch_id,test_date,test_id;

business_scenario: Find clients whose every production batches is Active.
solution_approach: I will use EXISTS to require that each clients has at least one production batches. I will use NOT EXISTS to exclude clients with a non-Active production batches.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name FROM clients m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM production_batches r WHERE r.client_id=m.client_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM production_batches r WHERE r.client_id=m.client_id AND r.status<>'Active') ORDER BY m.client_id;

business_scenario: Find production batches above the average batch_cost for their status.
solution_approach: I will compare each production batches with the average batch cost for its own status.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT batch_id,status,batch_cost FROM production_batches r WHERE batch_cost>(SELECT AVG(x.batch_cost) FROM production_batches x WHERE x.status=r.status) ORDER BY status,batch_cost DESC;

business_scenario: Calculate days between the first and last event for each production batches.
solution_approach: I will join production batches and test results, group by batch id and take minimum and maximum test date. I will subtract the first date from the last date to get active days.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id,MIN(e.test_date) first_event,MAX(e.test_date) last_event,MAX(e.test_date)-MIN(e.test_date) active_days FROM production_batches r JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Calculate every event's percentage contribution to its production batches total.
solution_approach: I will divide each test results amount by the total amount within its batch id partition.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT test_id,batch_id,amount,ROUND(100.0*amount/NULLIF(SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id),0),2) record_percent FROM test_results ORDER BY batch_id,test_id;

business_scenario: Return the highest-value clients in each segment.
solution_approach: I will join clients and production batches to total batch cost for every clients and segment. I will row-number within each segment and keep rank 1.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name,m.segment,SUM(r.batch_cost) total_amount FROM clients m JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id GROUP BY m.client_id,m.client_name,m.segment), ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total_amount DESC,client_id) rn FROM totals) SELECT client_id,client_name,segment,total_amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY segment;

business_scenario: Find test results whose amount is above their parent record average.
solution_approach: I will compare each test results amount with the average amount for its parent batch id.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT test_id,batch_id,amount FROM test_results e WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM test_results x WHERE x.batch_id=e.batch_id) ORDER BY batch_id,amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find clients whose record count is above the average master record count.
solution_approach: I will left join clients and production batches and count production batches for every clients in a CTE. I will keep clients counts above the average master count.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.client_id,m.client_name,COUNT(r.batch_id) record_count FROM clients m LEFT JOIN production_batches r ON m.client_id=r.client_id GROUP BY m.client_id,m.client_name) SELECT client_id,client_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,client_id;

business_scenario: Show completed, pending and failed event totals per production batches.
solution_approach: I will join production batches and test results to conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per production batches.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.batch_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Pending' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) pending_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) failed_amount FROM production_batches r LEFT JOIN test_results e ON r.batch_id=e.batch_id GROUP BY r.batch_id ORDER BY r.batch_id;

business_scenario: Return the latest test results row for every batch id.
solution_approach: I will row number test results partitioned by batch id from newest to oldest by test date and test id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: clients(client_id PK, client_name, city, segment, joined_date); chip_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); production_batches(batch_id PK, client_id FK, product_id FK, production_date, status, batch_cost); test_results(test_id PK, batch_id FK, test_date, test_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY batch_id ORDER BY test_date DESC,test_id DESC) rn FROM test_results e) SELECT test_id,batch_id,test_date,test_type,amount,status FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY batch_id;

business_scenario: Calculate completed and failed event amounts for every enrollments.
solution_approach: I will join enrollments and assessments and use CASE inside SUM for Completed and Failed event amounts.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.enrollment_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM enrollments r LEFT JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY r.enrollment_id ORDER BY r.enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Count assessments by calendar month.
solution_approach: I will derive the month from assessment date, group assessments and count each month.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',assessment_date)::date AS event_month,COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM assessments GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',assessment_date) ORDER BY event_month;

business_scenario: Find students with no enrollments.
solution_approach: I will left join enrollments to students on student id and keep students with no enrollments key.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.student_id,m.student_name FROM students m LEFT JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id WHERE r.enrollment_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.student_id;

business_scenario: Find courses items that are unused by enrollments.
solution_approach: I will left join enrollments to courses on course id and keep courses with no matching enrollments.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.course_id,c.course_name FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments r ON c.course_id=r.course_id WHERE r.enrollment_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.course_id;

business_scenario: Find the earliest enrollments date for every students.
solution_approach: I will join students and enrollments, group by student id and take the minimum enrollment date.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.student_id,m.student_name,MIN(r.enrollment_date) AS first_date FROM students m JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id GROUP BY m.student_id,m.student_name ORDER BY m.student_id;

business_scenario: Find the latest assessments date for every enrollments.
solution_approach: I will left join assessments to enrollments, group by enrollment id and take the maximum assessment date.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.enrollment_id,MAX(e.assessment_date) AS latest_event_date FROM enrollments r LEFT JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY r.enrollment_id ORDER BY r.enrollment_id;

business_scenario: List distinct students with at least one completed assessments.
solution_approach: I will join students, enrollments and assessments, keep Completed events and remove duplicate students.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.student_id,m.student_name FROM students m JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id WHERE e.status='Completed' ORDER BY m.student_id;

business_scenario: Calculate average event amount by courses category.
solution_approach: I will join courses, enrollments and assessments through their keys. I will group by category and average event amount.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT c.category,AVG(e.amount) AS average_event_amount FROM courses c JOIN enrollments r ON c.course_id=r.course_id JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY c.category ORDER BY c.category;

business_scenario: Count enrollments by master segment and record status.
solution_approach: I will join students and enrollments and group counts by segment and status.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.segment,r.status,COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM students m JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id GROUP BY m.segment,r.status ORDER BY m.segment,r.status;

business_scenario: Rank students by total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join students, enrollments and assessments and total event amounts per students. I will rank the totals from highest to lowest.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.student_id,m.student_name,SUM(e.amount) total_amount FROM students m JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY m.student_id,m.student_name) SELECT student_id,student_name,total_amount,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM totals ORDER BY amount_rank,student_id;

business_scenario: Find enrollments whose latest event was before 1 January 2026 or is missing.
solution_approach: I will left join assessments to enrollments using enrollment id so enrollments without activity remain. I will group each enrollments by enrollment id and use HAVING on its latest assessment date.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.enrollment_id,MAX(e.assessment_date) AS latest_event_date FROM enrollments r LEFT JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY r.enrollment_id HAVING MAX(e.assessment_date)<DATE '2026-01-01' OR MAX(e.assessment_date) IS NULL ORDER BY r.enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Find students whose total course_fee is above the average master total.
solution_approach: I will use a CTE to total course fee by student id in enrollments. I will keep students totals above the average total.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT student_id,SUM(course_fee) total_amount FROM enrollments GROUP BY student_id) SELECT student_id,total_amount FROM totals WHERE total_amount>(SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM totals) ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

business_scenario: Classify enrollments into High, Medium and Low amount bands.
solution_approach: I will classify enrollments using CASE with 100000 and 50000 course fee boundaries.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT enrollment_id,course_fee,CASE WHEN course_fee>=100000 THEN 'High' WHEN course_fee>=50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END amount_band FROM enrollments ORDER BY enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Show month-over-month event amount for every enrollments.
solution_approach: I will total event amounts in assessments by enrollment id and month in a CTE. I will use LAG partitioned by enrollment id and ordered by event month.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT enrollment_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',assessment_date)::date event_month,SUM(amount) monthly_amount FROM assessments GROUP BY enrollment_id,DATE_TRUNC('month',assessment_date)) SELECT enrollment_id,event_month,monthly_amount,LAG(monthly_amount) OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id ORDER BY event_month) previous_month_amount FROM monthly ORDER BY enrollment_id,event_month;

business_scenario: Calculate a running event total within every enrollments.
solution_approach: I will use a windowed SUM of amount in assessments partitioned by enrollment id and ordered by assessment date and assessment id.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT enrollment_id,assessment_id,assessment_date,amount,SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id ORDER BY assessment_date,assessment_id) running_amount FROM assessments ORDER BY enrollment_id,assessment_date,assessment_id;

business_scenario: Return the two largest assessments for every enrollment id.
solution_approach: I will assign row numbers within each enrollment id in assessments by descending amount. I will keep row numbers 1 and 2 for every enrollment id.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id ORDER BY amount DESC,assessment_id) rn FROM assessments e) SELECT assessment_id,enrollment_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY enrollment_id,rn;

business_scenario: Calculate each enrollments share of total event amount.
solution_approach: I will join enrollments and assessments to total amounts for each enrollments in a CTE. I will divide each enrollments total by the windowed grand total.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT r.enrollment_id,COALESCE(SUM(e.amount),0) total_amount FROM enrollments r LEFT JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY r.enrollment_id) SELECT enrollment_id,total_amount,ROUND(100.0*total_amount/NULLIF(SUM(total_amount) OVER(),0),2) percent_of_total FROM totals ORDER BY enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Dense-rank enrollments by course_fee within each students.
solution_approach: I will dense rank enrollments within each student id by descending course fee.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT student_id,enrollment_id,course_fee,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY course_fee DESC) amount_rank FROM enrollments ORDER BY student_id,amount_rank,enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Show each event amount beside the previous event amount.
solution_approach: I will use LAG in assessments partitioned by enrollment id ordered by assessment date and assessment id.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT enrollment_id,assessment_id,assessment_date,amount,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id ORDER BY assessment_date,assessment_id) previous_amount FROM assessments ORDER BY enrollment_id,assessment_date,assessment_id;

business_scenario: Calculate a three-event moving average for each enrollments.
solution_approach: I will average the current and two preceding amounts in assessments partitioned by enrollment id ordered by assessment date and assessment id.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT enrollment_id,assessment_id,assessment_date,amount,AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id ORDER BY assessment_date,assessment_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) moving_average FROM assessments ORDER BY enrollment_id,assessment_date,assessment_id;

business_scenario: Find students whose every enrollments is Active.
solution_approach: I will use EXISTS to require that each students has at least one enrollments. I will use NOT EXISTS to exclude students with a non-Active enrollments.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT m.student_id,m.student_name FROM students m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM enrollments r WHERE r.student_id=m.student_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM enrollments r WHERE r.student_id=m.student_id AND r.status<>'Active') ORDER BY m.student_id;

business_scenario: Find enrollments above the average course_fee for their status.
solution_approach: I will compare each enrollments with the average course fee for its own status.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT enrollment_id,status,course_fee FROM enrollments r WHERE course_fee>(SELECT AVG(x.course_fee) FROM enrollments x WHERE x.status=r.status) ORDER BY status,course_fee DESC;

business_scenario: Calculate days between the first and last event for each enrollments.
solution_approach: I will join enrollments and assessments, group by enrollment id and take minimum and maximum assessment date. I will subtract the first date from the last date to get active days.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.enrollment_id,MIN(e.assessment_date) first_event,MAX(e.assessment_date) last_event,MAX(e.assessment_date)-MIN(e.assessment_date) active_days FROM enrollments r JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY r.enrollment_id ORDER BY r.enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Calculate every event's percentage contribution to its enrollments total.
solution_approach: I will divide each assessments amount by the total amount within its enrollment id partition.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT assessment_id,enrollment_id,amount,ROUND(100.0*amount/NULLIF(SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id),0),2) record_percent FROM assessments ORDER BY enrollment_id,assessment_id;

business_scenario: Return the highest-value students in each segment.
solution_approach: I will join students and enrollments to total course fee for every students and segment. I will row-number within each segment and keep rank 1.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.student_id,m.student_name,m.segment,SUM(r.course_fee) total_amount FROM students m JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id GROUP BY m.student_id,m.student_name,m.segment), ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total_amount DESC,student_id) rn FROM totals) SELECT student_id,student_name,segment,total_amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY segment;

business_scenario: Find assessments whose amount is above their parent record average.
solution_approach: I will compare each assessments amount with the average amount for its parent enrollment id.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT assessment_id,enrollment_id,amount FROM assessments e WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM assessments x WHERE x.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id) ORDER BY enrollment_id,amount DESC;

business_scenario: Find students whose record count is above the average master record count.
solution_approach: I will left join students and enrollments and count enrollments for every students in a CTE. I will keep students counts above the average master count.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.student_id,m.student_name,COUNT(r.enrollment_id) record_count FROM students m LEFT JOIN enrollments r ON m.student_id=r.student_id GROUP BY m.student_id,m.student_name) SELECT student_id,student_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,student_id;

business_scenario: Show completed, pending and failed event totals per enrollments.
solution_approach: I will join enrollments and assessments to conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per enrollments.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT r.enrollment_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Pending' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) pending_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) failed_amount FROM enrollments r LEFT JOIN assessments e ON r.enrollment_id=e.enrollment_id GROUP BY r.enrollment_id ORDER BY r.enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Return the latest assessments row for every enrollment id.
solution_approach: I will row number assessments partitioned by enrollment id from newest to oldest by assessment date and assessment id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: students(student_id PK, student_name, city, segment, joined_date); courses(course_id PK, course_name, category, status, base_value); enrollments(enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, status, course_fee); assessments(assessment_id PK, enrollment_id FK, assessment_date, assessment_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY enrollment_id ORDER BY assessment_date DESC,assessment_id DESC) rn FROM assessments e) SELECT assessment_id,enrollment_id,assessment_date,assessment_type,amount,status FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY enrollment_id;

business_scenario: Filter open customer orders with Active fulfillment status.

business_scenario: Find high-value customer orders where order total is greater than 50000 for VIP courier delivery.

business_scenario: List retail shoppers located in Chennai for regional warehouse delivery routing.

business_scenario: Count total retail customer orders placed through the e-commerce store.

business_scenario: Show customer orders sorted from highest to lowest order total.

business_scenario: List distinct product merchandise categories sold across the retail store catalog.

business_scenario: Find retail orders placed on or after 1 January 2026.
solution_approach: I will filter orders with order date on or after 1 January 2026.

business_scenario: Find order item transactions categorized as Sale.

answer_sql: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE item_type = 'Sale';

business_scenario: Return the first five registered shoppers by customer ID.
solution_approach: I will order by customer id and limit the result to five rows.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); orders(order_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, order_date, status, order_total); order_items(order_item_id PK, order_id FK, item_date, item_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM customers ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 5;

business_scenario: Find orders with order totals between 25000 and 75000 for commercial bulk discount eligibility.
solution_approach: I will keep orders whose order total is between 25000 and 75000.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); orders(order_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, order_date, status, order_total); order_items(order_item_id PK, order_id FK, item_date, item_type, quantity, amount, status)
answer_sql: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_total BETWEEN 25000 AND 75000;

business_scenario: Find retail customers whose name starts with A for loyalty program search.
solution_approach: I will use a prefix match to keep customers names starting with A.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); orders(order_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, order_date, status, order_total); order_items(order_item_id PK, order_id FK, item_date, item_type, quantity, amount, status)

business_scenario: Return customer orders that are either Active or Pending payment verification.
solution_approach: I will keep orders when status is either Active or Pending.

business_scenario: List retail shoppers in the Premium VIP loyalty tier.
